name: Washte Pawne
summary: Across the southern Barrens, Washte Pawne's feather leaves hunters with a pain they carry to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. For the tauren, the hunt becomes a trial of regret.

sections.title: The Spirit Biter
sections.body: Thunderhawks are hard to find in the Barrens, and the nomadic tribes honor them. In Taurahe, Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter.” Its death is no ordinary hunt. Shamans whisper that striking down a thunderhawk may bring triumph or misfortune.

sections.title: A Lesson in Regret
sections.body: After Washte Pawne falls, its feather burns against the skin with a pain that lingers. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer explains that the ache is regret, not poison. Taking a magnificent life carries a burden. The hunter must face that sorrow and turn it into lasting wisdom.

faq.answer: In Taurahe, the language of the tauren, Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter.” The name belongs to a rare thunderhawk that soars over the southern Barrens.

faq.q: Why does Washte Pawne's feather cause pain?
faq.answer: Jorn Skyseer says the feather's sting is the sharp pain of regret. It reflects the spiritual cost of ending a magnificent creature's life.

faq.q: Who do I bring Washte Pawne's Feather to?
faq.answer: Bring the feather to Jorn Skyseer, a tauren elder at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens.

faq.q: What omen does slaying a thunderhawk bring?
faq.answer: Tauren tradition says a thunderhawk's death can herald great fortune or immense doom. Jorn says Washte Pawne's fall brings neither fate by itself; the hunter must make wisdom from remorse.
Washte Pawne roams the skies of the southern Barrens, often circling the savannah near Camp Taurajo.

faq.q: What does Jorn Skyseer think of you after slaying it?
faq.answer: Jorn does not condemn you. He sees that bearing the quill's pain means you have mastered regret and turned spiritual grief into strength and understanding.

angles.text: For the Shu'halo, taking Spirit Biter's life teaches respect for nature's balance. It asks you to turn regret into inner wisdom.
Facing Washte Pawne tests your motives as a hunter. Taking a beast's life carries weight beyond a trophy.
The thunderhawk's lingering sting reveals the wild's spiritual force. As a shaman, you can recognize its resonance with elemental harmonies.
At Camp Taurajo, you find a spiritual and hunting crossroads for the Horde. Young warriors face tests of conscience and martial skill.
